title: 搭建场景

sentenceFrames.pattern: ：This goes back to [time] when I was [situation].
sentenceFrames.usage: 故事的开场。"Goes back to" 比 "happened in" 更有故事感。
sentenceFrames.example: This goes back to about 3 years ago when I was living in Shanghai and didn't really know what I wanted to do with my life.
substitutions: This goes back to **when I was in college**. I was _____.
This goes back to **my first job**. I had just _____.
This goes back to **a trip I took to _____**. I was traveling alone and _____.
你的一个真实故事：This goes back to _____ when I was _____.

sentenceFrames.usage: 用一句话帮听众"看到"场景。故事高手都用这招。
sentenceFrames.example: Picture this: it's 11 PM on a Tuesday, I'm in a tiny hotel room in a city I don't know, my phone just died, and I have no idea where my passport is.
substitutions: Picture this: **your first day at a new job.** It's... You're... The room is...
Picture this: **a busy train station during Spring Festival.** People are... The air is... You can hear...
Picture this: **your most embarrassing moment.** You're standing there... Everyone is looking at you... Your face feels...
你自己的故事：Picture this: _____. It's _____. You're _____. You can hear/smell/feel _____.

sentenceFrames.pattern: ：The thing you have to understand is [backstory].
sentenceFrames.usage: 讲故事前给必要的背景信息，让听众明白"为什么这很重要"。
sentenceFrames.example: The thing you have to understand is, I had never traveled alone before this trip. I was the kind of person who always had a plan, always had a backup. So when I found myself completely lost...
substitutions: 为什么决定换工作：The thing you have to understand is, _____.
为什么那天特别重要：The thing you have to understand is, _____.
关于你要讲的故事：The thing you have to understand is, _____.
